answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The nectar multiplier is published, charged in fable, and glacier lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 762 identities would post 1990 proofs and burn roughly 60 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
